newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHT - Weider seen as fast grower.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHT - Weider seen as fast grower.

text.p: Fast-growing Weider Nutrition International Inc, a leading maker of diet supplements for bodybuilders, is muscling its way into the stock market with a 5.6 million share offering.

Weider's sales growth resulted from a broadening of scope that took its products beyond bodybuilding and into the realms of diet products and sports nutrition, said Linda Killian, a portfolio manager at Renaissance Capital of Greenwich, Conn.
Despite strong sales growth and impressive margins throughout the nutritional supplements industry, Killian said, "Stocks in this area have not been doing well."

Ryan Jacob, director of research at the IPO Value Monitor, said he expects Weider Nutrition, the food supplement and vitamin unit of Weider Health and Fitness, to price within the $13.50 to $16.50 range in the middle of the week and open at a slight premium.
Jacob was similarly optimistic about Weider rival, TwinLabs Corp.

Weider's sales for the nine months ended February 28, 1997, reached $151.4 million and net income totaled $8.1 million, including a charge of $2.1 million for the impairment of intangible assets under an accounting standard change.

Few companies in the food supplement business have the strong brand names and loyal customers that Weider has, Jacob said. Many of the customers are not price sensitive about the products, leading to the high margins, he added.
Weider has been associated with bodybuilding since 1940, when fitness expert Joe Weider started the company.
After the offering, there will be 8.2 million shares of class A common stock and 15.6 million class B shares.
Proceeds will be used to repay existing debt and pay a one time dividend to the parent company.
Weider Health and Fitness, which publishes magazines and makes exercise equipment, will have 95 percent voting control and 65.6 percent of the number of shares of the company.
Killian said Weider Health's publishing division has been an active tool in promoting all of Weider's products.
Weider's prospectus said it intends to pay dividends of $0.15 a share annually, or $0.0375 a share per quarter.
"Eventually the investors will come around and realize these companies are growing well and give impressive margins," Killian said about the nutrition supplement industry.
While it did not post huge gains, TwinLabs is trading at 13-3/4 after pricing at $12 a share in its November initial public offering.
"It's a very solid company, and generally we haven't seen a lot of solid companies come out this year," Jacob said.
For the year ended May 31, 1996, Weider Nutrition reported sales of $186.4 million and net income of $15.0 million. In fiscal 1995, the company had $90.9 million in sales.
